title: Clean a wireless earbud and replace its silicone eartip
instruction: Remove the worn eartip and put it in the discard cup. Dry-brush the speaker mesh, clean the charging contacts with the cotton swab, then fit the new eartip. Leave the earbud and tools released.
context: Wireless earbuds need periodic dry cleaning and their silicone tips wear out or must be changed for fit. The complete service procedure combines small-part removal, choosing the correct cleaning implement for each surface, controlled contact-and-sliding, and seating a compliant replacement around a narrow nozzle.
setup: One black wireless earbud (Samsung Galaxy Buds+ envelope 22.5 x 17.5 x 19.2 mm, 6.3 g) sits nozzle-forward in a low silicone service cradle on a 340 x 400 x 4 mm inspection mat; the cradle holds the shell still and leaves the nozzle and top exposed. A worn grey silicone eartip is fitted on the nozzle. Fourteen 1 mm (1.1 mm in the simulator) dry soil dots of blue chalk-line marking chalk (calcium carbonate; e.g. IRWIN Strait-Line 64902 refill) mark the surfaces to clean: 8 on a 5 mm circle on the speaker mesh and 3 on each of the two gold charging contacts on top, laid through the stencils in the reset notes (the simulator renders them brown; colour is not scored). A dry detail brush (100 x 40 x 32 mm rubberised handle, offset nylon bristle head) lies on a raised service-tray ledge behind the earbud, held by a light clip that lets go once the brush is gripped. A reusable electronics swab (90 x 20 x 20 mm handle, cotton tip at each end) lies beside it. A fresh pale-blue eartip stands on a small presentation peg at the lower left; a 60 mm, 25 mm deep discard cup is at the lower right. No case, liquid, putty or sharp tool.
scoring: Cleaning is recorded over the episode only while the correct tool is within a 2.5 mm contact band of its surface and sliding across it: the brush's bristle tips across the speaker mesh, and a cotton tip across the charging-contact zone. Hovering, or the wrong tool, earns nothing. At least 80% of each soil set must be cleared. End-state ladder: 0.15 for the worn tip off the nozzle and inside the discard cup; 0.40 for that plus the mesh clean; 0.60 for that plus the contacts clean; 0.85 for that plus the fresh tip caught and seated within 2 mm of the nozzle base; 1.0 for all of that with both grippers at least 4 cm from the earbud, tips and tools and every loose object at rest. Pulling the fresh tip back off loses the fit credit. On a real station the specks are counted from photos taken from a fixed phone stand under the same light before and after the trial (nozzle face at 10 cm, contacts from above): a speck is cleared when, with its stencil laid back on, its hole shows no chalk; at least 7 of 8 mesh and 5 of 6 contact specks are needed, and they count only if the video shows the brush on the mesh and the swab on the contacts.
reset_notes: Refit the worn tip on the nozzle, put the fresh tip back on its peg, return the brush to its ledge and the swab to its mark, and empty the discard cup. Soil (about 2 min): wipe the mesh and contacts clean with a dry microfibre cloth; lay the mesh stencil (7.4 mm disc of 0.1 mm transparency film, eight 1 mm punched holes at 45 deg spacing on a 5 mm circle) on the nozzle face and the contact stencil (three 1 mm holes per pad at -1.2/0, +0.8/-1.0 and +0.8/+1.0 mm from each pad centre, x toward the nozzle) over the pads; dab once through each stencil with a cosmetic sponge pressed into the chalk, lift it straight off, and photograph both faces from the fixed phone stand to confirm all 14 dots. Tap and wipe the chalk off the brush and swab tips and wipe the tool handles.
fidelity: Rigid-body Isaac Sim 6.1/PhysX at 20 Hz. Earbud size and mass follow Samsung's published Buds+ data; the earbud, tools and tips are compound primitives and the earbud is held fixed by its cradle. Silicone stretch is a compliant axial capture joint (catches within 6 mm and 30 deg, 0.8 mm play, about 1.5 N to pull on or off); these values are estimates, not measured. Cleaning is a one-way record of correct-tool contact plus sliding; soil specks vanish as stroke thresholds are passed.
